assumptions: ODRL artifacts are available as machine-readable policy objects or references to them.
The consuming system can distinguish policy publication from policy evaluation and policy enforcement.
Ecosystem-specific ODRL profiles disclose any custom actions, constraints, or party functions needed for interpretation.
An ODRL policy object or stable reference, a profile or vocabulary reference for non-core terms, and supporting evaluator output are available when policy enforcement claims are material.
prohibitedInferences: Do not infer runtime enforcement merely because an ODRL policy is published.
Do not infer that ODRL permission statements create delegated authority across agents unless a separate delegation mechanism says so.
Do not infer that all TSMM trust objects are reducible to ODRL asset usage semantics.
comparisonNotes: ODRL is strongest when used as the policy-expression layer for content, services, disclosure, and access constraints.
TSMM remains the broader semantic layer for governance, assurance, evidence, assessment, and trust effects.
validationHints: Check that profile references and target identifiers are stable and resolvable.
Check that policy targets, parties, and duties map cleanly to the modeled trust surface.
Check that downstream repos do not silently equate policy references with enforcement proof.
